q8.answer: The commit's merge step inserts a staged order if it is new. If it already exists, it replaces the stored row only when the staged updated_at is equal to or later than the stored one, so an older copy from the lookback overlap or a re-run can never overwrite a newer one. A re-run writes the same values, so it does no harm.

q9.answer: The high-water mark is stored in ctl.pipeline_state as hwm_ts. It is set to the run's window_hi (02:00 UTC on run_date), and only if the stored value is lower. It is written only inside the commit transaction, after the merge, in the same transaction that marks the attempt's row committed, so it moves only when the night's data has loaded.

q10.answer: Dashboards read only mart.fact_orders, and only at their 06:00 UTC refresh. The merge, the hwm_ts move and the committed mark are one warehouse transaction, so a half-loaded night is never visible: if the commit fails before COMMIT, all of it rolls back. This depends on the warehouse supporting atomic multi-statement transactions, which is listed as an open question, and whether dashboards also query live between refreshes is still open.

q11.answer: Nothing from the failed attempt is reused. Its staging table is dropped by the failure handler or, if the process died, by the next attempt's preflight before extract. The retry re-extracts from the replica into a fresh staging table, using the same window_lo and window_hi that attempt 1 stored on the latest runs row.

q12.answer: Reconciliation re-reads day D from the replica, taking rows created on D with updated_at at most window_hi and ignoring order_ids updated after window_hi. It applies them with the same stage, check and merge steps as the nightly load, so the newer-updated_at rule still holds. It does not move hwm_ts and writes no ctl.pipeline_runs row, because a reload is not an attempt; its result goes only to ctl.recon_results.
